builtins.protocol: LSL: discovery by resolve, liblsl StreamInlet (pylsl), stream XML metadata
builtins.modality_note: Not declared by the adapter (modality is null). Stream type and channel metadata are the producer's statements; BrainOS cannot verify the origin and labels it 'Live stream, origin unverified'.

read_only.statement: Receive-only: StreamInlet only; BrainOS never creates an outlet for, or sends to, a producer.

evidence.description: Discovery, metadata, units, timestamps, gaps, composite clocks, reconnect when the outlet returns (M3-AT-1..4).
evidence.protocol_reference: Genuine liblsl outlets (pylsl StreamOutlet) consumed through discovery and StreamInlet; no mocks

evidence.description: Real FALCON H1 blocks streamed over LSL, declared prerecorded: every bin arrives once and decoded output equals the offline decoder bin for bin.
evidence.protocol_reference: Genuine liblsl outlets publishing recorded human data, declared prerecorded

evidence.description: Throughput, latency and loss with the publisher in a separate process (scripts/bench_live.py); no hardware involved.
evidence.anchor: Publishers run in a separate process

not_tested: Third-party LSL producers (vendor LSL apps, LabRecorder interop).
Acquisition hardware: level 3 needs a real amplifier's LSL app recorded at the same time by a reference recorder (LabRecorder to XDF), with counts, values and timestamps compared offline.
limitations: BrainOS cannot verify whether an LSL stream comes from hardware, a file player or a simulator.

builtins.protocol: Open Ephys GUI ZMQ Interface plugin wire format (pyzmq SUB; heartbeat on the plugin's REP port)
builtins.modality_note: Not declared by the adapter (modality is null). BrainOS cannot tell whether the GUI reads hardware, a file or a simulator.

read_only.statement: Receive-only (ZMQ SUB). The single documented exception is the plugin's heartbeat, a liveness message so the GUI lists BrainOS as a client (docs/OPEN_EPHYS.md).

evidence.description: Data, TTL and spike messages, heartbeat, block assembly and loss counters over real ZMQ sockets (M3-AT-5, M3-AT-6).
evidence.protocol_reference: The ZMQ Interface plugin's official Python client (plot_process_zmq.py, pinned by SHA-256, downloaded at test time) parses BrainOS's test publisher bit-exactly

evidence.description: Protocol facts derived line by line from the plugin source; limitations.
Open Ephys wire format from a publisher in a separate process (scripts/bench_live.py); no hardware involved.

not_tested: Never run against the Open Ephys GUI or an acquisition board: the test publisher reproduces the plugin's format from its source, so a mismatch with the real plugin binary is possible.
Level 3 needs the GUI with an acquisition board, compared against the GUI's own Binary-format recording, with TTL alignment checked against a known pulse generator.
limitations: Data that arrives while open() learns the layout is not emitted, also after every reconnect.
The plugin may truncate non-ASCII channel names in its JSON header.

plugins.protocol: Adapter SDK plugin that generates synthetic motor-imagery EEG in its own process (declared synthetic)

read_only.statement: Receive-only: the adapter SDK's SourcePlugin / SourceSession interface has no write, stimulate or command method, and the plugin runs in a separate plugin-host process.

evidence.description: The plugin run exactly as BrainOS runs it (separate host process, BrainOS's validation), using only the adapter SDK.
evidence.anchor: Tests a plugin author would write

evidence.description: Discovered by a real server, configured over REST, streamed over the WebSocket, recorded, replayed and reconnected after its host process is killed.
Milestone 4 demonstration: pipeline, LDA calibration and command-router authorization with this adapter (declared synthetic).

not_tested: Not applicable beyond software: a declared-synthetic generator for tutorials, never brain data.
limitations: Synthetic signal (mu-band desynchronisation at C3/C4 by construction); not physiologically validated.

plugins.protocol: BrainFlow BoardShim (official library) in the plugin host: synthetic, playback-file and streaming boards; other BoardIds boards by option

read_only.statement: Receive-only: the adapter SDK has no write method, and BrainFlow board configuration (config_board, gain, impedance modes) is deliberately not offered because it writes to the device.

evidence.description: Metadata equals get_board_descr; 3 s of streaming through the public API with every contract rule checked; rate and unix timestamps.
evidence.protocol_reference: Official BrainFlow library, BoardShim SYNTHETIC_BOARD; no mocks

evidence.description: Every value played back equals DataFilter.read_file of the same file bit for bit; deleted samples appear as a gap; counter wrap is not loss.
evidence.protocol_reference: Official BrainFlow PLAYBACK_FILE_BOARD replaying a file written by DataFilter.write_file

evidence.description: Every sample received over multicast equals the producer's sample exactly; stopping the producer gives LinkLost.
evidence.protocol_reference: A second official BoardShim session publishing with add_streamer to the plugin's STREAMING_BOARD

evidence.description: Invalid options; a real BrainFlow driver (CYTON_BOARD) on a nonexistent serial port fails with OpenFailed.
Every board description shipped with the installed BrainFlow maps cleanly; never invasive=True.
Through the plugin host and the unchanged runtime with the synthetic board.
Rate and latency measurement script; results (synthetic and streaming boards, machine-dependent) in docs/ECOSYSTEMS.md.
Mapping, clock, loss, what was tested and what was not.

not_tested: No hardware board was connected; units, channel types and package counters of real boards come from BrainFlow's descriptions only.
hardware_tested needs a physical BrainFlow-supported board and an operator-signed attestation; level 3 also needs a comparison against an independent reference recording.
limitations: Only BrainFlow's DEFAULT preset rows are read; BrainFlow markers cannot reach the plugin.
prerecorded cannot be detected for a streaming board whose producer replays a file.

plugins.protocol: BCI2000 App Connector ConnectorOutput (UDP, one ASCII line per datagram): processed control information, never raw signal

read_only.statement: Receive-only: ConnectorOutput only; never ConnectorInput, Operator scripting or BCI2000Remote (write and control paths). The control signal reaches apps as a command only if the operator enables the command router.

evidence.description: Opt-in live test: the plugin receives a genuine BCI2000 build's own ConnectorOutput (131 control blocks, 0 malformed, 0 dropped, 5 state changes in order).
evidence.protocol_reference: Genuine BCI2000 3.6 built from source: SignalGenerator, DummySignalProcessing, DummyApplication's own ConnectorOutput

evidence.description: UDP replay of 2 011 datagrams captured from that build with original timing (values equal the transmitted text); options, layout changes, port handling.
Strict line grammar, block boundaries, loss, reordering and SourceTime wrap against a byte-for-byte reproduction of ConnectorOutput.
Recorded BCI2000 output through the plugin host and the unchanged runtime; no application command by itself.
Block rate and latency against genuine BCI2000; results (machine-dependent) in docs/ECOSYSTEMS.md.
Interfaces, mapping, clock and loss; a receiver gap of about 1 s stops BCI2000's output until the next run (measured).

not_tested: No amplifier and no BCI2000 source module other than SignalGenerator; no application other than DummyApplication; BCI2000 on Windows or macOS, or on another machine.

protocol_tested in a certification report: needs a live BCI2000 run, and BCI2000 stops sending for the rest of a run after its receiver is unreachable for about 1 s, so the certifier's kill and reopen phases need a run restart.
The official bci2000.org distribution: the build is from a public fork's source.
limitations: Processed control information only, never raw signal.
A block whose datagrams are all lost is undetectable (no block counter on the wire).
synthetic and prerecorded are operator declarations.
